Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a topological
space and let $k$ be a field. The category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces is the category of modules over the ringed space
$(X,k_X)$ with constant structure sheaf $k_X$
([[def-locally-ringed-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is a locally
small Grothendieck category and carries a functorial injective embedding, and
iterating that embedding on cokernels yields for every $k$-sheaf one specific
injective resolution
([[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]). These resolutions are
bounded-below injective replacements, so with the dependent choice supplied by
AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) the bounded-below
injective complexes model the bounded derived category:
$K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))\to
D^+(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is an equivalence, and morphisms of the bounded
derived category are computed by these replacements
([[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]).

Now let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety and let
$\mathfrak S$ be a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier
condition of $X$
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Let
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ be the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are bounded
and constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$
([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Then
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory: it is closed under
shifts, isomorphisms and mapping cones. More generally, if two bounded
algebraically constructible complexes are constructible with respect to one
common finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, then their cone is
bounded and constructible with respect to that stratification.

on $X$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]).
Write $\mathcal F|_U:=j^{-1}\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F|_Z:=i^{-1}\mathcal F$ for
the restrictions ([[def-restriction-sheaf-open-subspace]]). Then:

1. the adjoint transpose of the identity of $\mathcal F|_U$ under the adjunction
   of [[thm-extension-by-zero-adjunction-exactness]] and the unit of the
   adjunction ([[thm-inverse-direct-image-adjunction]]) fit into a short exact
   sequence of sheaves of abelian groups on $X$
   $$0\to j_!(\mathcal F|_U)\to\mathcal F\to i_*(\mathcal F|_Z)\to0,$$
   where $j_!$ is extension by zero ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]]) and
   $i_*$ is the direct image ([[def-direct-image-sheaf]],
   [[lem-direct-image-is-sheaf]]); exactness is that of
   [[def-exact-sequence-sheaves]];
2. if $\mathcal F=\mathbb Z_X$ is the constant sheaf with value $\mathbb Z$ on
   $X$, then $\mathcal F|_U$ is canonically isomorphic to the constant sheaf
   $\mathbb Z_U$ on $U$, so the sequence of clause 1 reads
   $0\to j_!(\mathbb Z_U)\to\mathbb Z_X\to i_*(\mathcal F|_Z)\to0$ up to that
   canonical isomorphism.

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of a closed subset
$Z\subseteq X$ carrying the subspace topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]), and
let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $X$
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]])
whose stalks vanish off $Z$, that is $\mathcal G_x=0$ for every $x\in X\setminus Z$
([[def-stalk-of-presheaf]]). Then the unit
$$\eta:\mathcal G\longrightarrow i_*i^{-1}\mathcal G$$
of the adjunction ([[thm-inverse-direct-image-adjunction]]) between inverse image
and direct image ([[def-direct-image-sheaf]], [[lem-direct-image-is-sheaf]]) is an
isomorphism of sheaves of abelian groups; equivalently
$\mathcal G\cong i_*(\mathcal G|_Z)$ under the identification
$\mathcal G|_Z=i^{-1}\mathcal G$ ([[def-restriction-sheaf-open-subspace]]).

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace.

1. For every sheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal F$ on $U$ and every sheaf of
   abelian groups $\mathcal G$ on $X$, there is a natural bijection
   $$\operatorname{Hom}_X(j_!\mathcal F,\mathcal G) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_U(\mathcal F,j^{-1}\mathcal G).$$
2. The functor $j_!$ is exact on sheaves of abelian groups.

Let $f:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ be a chain map in an additive category. The
**mapping cone** of $f$ is the chain complex $\operatorname{Cone}(f)_\bullet$
whose degree-$n$ term is
$$\operatorname{Cone}(f)_n:=D_n\oplus C[1]_n=D_n\oplus C_{n-1},$$
and whose differential is
$$d_n^{\operatorname{Cone}(f)}(y,x):=(d_n^D(y)+f_{n-1}(x),-d_{n-1}^C(x)).$$

Thus $\operatorname{Cone}(f)$ is the direct sum of $D$ and the shift $C[1]$ as
a graded object, with the off-diagonal term given by $f$.

The derived category, with shift $[1]$ and distinguished triangles the isomorphic images of cone triangles, is triangulated. The localization functor $Q$ is exact. Every such triangle gives a long exact cohomology sequence $\cdots\to H^n(X)\to H^n(Y)\to H^n(Z)\to H^{n+1}(X)\to\cdots$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: A sheaf on the one-point space is its vector space of global sections, so a bounded complex of $k$-sheaves on the point is a bounded complex of $k$-vector spaces, and the unique finite smooth stratification of the point makes constructibility with respect to it exactly the condition that every cohomology space be finite-dimensional by [F1]. A bounded complex whose cohomology is finite-dimensional is isomorphic in the derived category to a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces: truncate to the finite interval between the lowest and highest degrees in which cohomology is nonzero, and split the resulting bounded complex into the direct sum of its cohomology spaces placed in their degrees, using that every short exact sequence of vector spaces splits. Both sides are therefore equivalent to the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional vector spaces, with morphisms computed by the injective models of [F2].

On the point inverse and direct image of the identity are exact identity functors, and every section has compact support, so the proper-support functor is also the exact identity. Their derived functors are therefore identities. In the exceptional candidate of [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]], the fibre opens are only the point and the empty set; compact sections are exact, giving dimension bound $d=0$, and the constant sheaf $k$ is itself $c$-soft, so take $K=k[0]$. For a bounded finite-dimensional complex $B$ every term is injective over $k$, and the candidate has sections $\operatorname{Hom}_k^\bullet(k,B)=B$ on the point and zero on the empty set. Thus $f^!$ is the identity with its ordinary evaluation adjunction, and $\omega_{\operatorname{pt}}=a_{\operatorname{pt}}^!k=k[0]$. The ordinary-operations lemma [[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]] identifies tensor and internal Hom with the finite signed complexes: $(A\otimes B)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}A^p\otimes_kB^q$, with $d(a\otimes b)=d_Aa\otimes b+(-1)^pa\otimes d_Bb$, and $\mathcal Hom^n(A,B)=\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_k(A^p,B^{p+n})$, with $d\varphi=d_B\varphi-(-1)^n\varphi d_A$. Their terms and amplitudes are finite, so they belong to the category identified in step 1.1. Here $f_*$ and $f_!$ in the Example denote their derived operations, which coincide with their exact underived functors in this case.

Apply [F3] to the constant sheaf $\mathcal F=k_{\mathbb C}$ on $X=\mathbb C$, with $U=\mathbb C^*$ and $Z=\{0\}$: the restriction $k_{\mathbb C}|_{\mathbb C^*}$ is the constant sheaf $k_{\mathbb C^*}$, the restriction to the closed point is $k$, and the sequence reads $0\to j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}\to k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k\to0$, the terms being computed by [F5] for the extension by zero. Stalkwise the middle sheaf is exact: at $x\neq0$ the stalk of $j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}$ is $k$ and the stalk of $i_*k$ is $0$, while at $0$ the first stalk is $0$ and the last is $k$; the quotient of $k_{\mathbb C}$ by $j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}$ has no stalks off $\{0\}$, and by [F4] it is canonically the pushforward $i_*k$ of its restriction to the closed point. All maps are $k$-linear, since they are obtained from the canonical adjunction units of [F5] applied to $k$-sheaves.

View $k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k$ as a chain map of complexes concentrated in degree $0$, and let $C$ be its mapping cone with the convention of [F6], so $C^{-1}=k_{\mathbb C}$, $C^0=i_*k$ and the differential $C^{-1}\to C^0$ is the map of step 2.2. Its cohomology is $H^{-1}(C)=\ker(k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k)=j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}$ by the exactness of step 2.2 and $H^0(C)=\operatorname{coker}(k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k)=0$, so $C$ is quasi-isomorphic to $j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}[1]$, since the two complexes have the same single nonzero cohomology sheaf in degree $-1$. By the rotation property of cone triangles in [F7], the triangle $k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k\to C\to k_{\mathbb C}[1]$ is isomorphic to the distinguished triangle $j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}\to k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k\to j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}[1]$, the ordinary localization triangle of the open subset $\mathbb C^*$; all three sheaves are constructible for the two-stratum stratification $\{\mathbb C^*,\{0\}\}$ of the line, so the triangle lies in $D_c^b(\mathbb C;k)$ by [F1].
